title: THE GIANT WHO REFUSED TO BE RESCUED
deck: Illuminara breaks open a buried engine chamber and finds Oru, the stone giant whose breathing powers six hospitals. He refuses to leave. With nine hours before the damaged turbines stop, she must protect the patients, expose the city's old crime and make staying unnecessary—without turning liberation into one more order given to him.
shape: Five scenes move from Illuminara's mistaken rescue and Oru's refusal, through somatic listening that reveals how his breathing and the city's forgotten compressed-air and geothermal systems can share one pressure rhythm, into a public confrontation where Oru rejects both official concealment and activist ownership of his freedom. A failed hospital transfer forces Oru, patients, crews and activists to correct the bridge together. Once all six hospitals run without his body, Oru freely chooses limited transition work, claims an independent home and later returns as a healer rather than an engine.

scenes.title: The Wall That Opened
paragraphs: *Cauldron Nine beneath the city of Vale · Nine hours before hospital reserve exhaustion*

Illuminara tore the last iron rib from the buried wall and caught three hundred tonnes of cracked masonry before it could fall inward. Cold air rushed past her into a chamber built around a sleeping body.

The giant was forty metres long. Dark stone plates rose and fell along his chest. With every breath, six bronze bellows beside him compressed. Far above, six hospitals took the pulse through pipes older than any living engineer.
The restraint rings around his wrists had rusted open generations ago. Their scars had not.

Rava Sen, leader of the Open Earth collective, climbed over the broken sill with a red liberation cord around her arm. Behind her came Director Kes from the city energy office and Dr Anik Ilyan, elected by the six hospital patient councils.

**Rava**  
Oru, the wall is open. You can come out.
The giant's eyes opened like two lamps behind rain-dark glass.

**Oru**  
Close it.
A pressure alarm began to howl. Illuminara felt the broken chamber losing the dense air that made the bellows efficient. Each breath now delivered less force than the one before.

**Illuminara**  
I believed this was an active prison. I opened it before I asked you.

**Oru**  
Yes.
She waited. An apology that hurried toward forgiveness would only ask him to carry her discomfort too.

**Illuminara**  
I am sorry. I will repair what I broke. I will not touch you again without your permission.

**Kes**  
The west seal cannot be restored in time. At current leakage the hospital turbines fall below safe output in nine hours.

**Rava**  
Then evacuate the hospitals. We are not putting him back in a cage because your city made slavery convenient.

**Dr Anik**  
Four hundred patients cannot be moved. Thirty-two are on blood oxygenators. You may call that convenience after you have carried them through the upper tunnels.
Rava flinched, but did not retreat.

**Rava**  
And how many more centuries do you prescribe for him?
Oru placed one palm against the chamber floor. The turbines answered with a low, steady vibration.

**Oru**  
I prescribe nothing. I am not your patient.

**Illuminara**  
What do you want in the next nine hours?

**Oru**  
The children breathing. The truth spoken. No one using my departure as proof that they have finally understood me.
Kes stared at the open restraints rather than at Oru.

**Kes**  
The current arrangement was ratified eighty-three times.

**Oru**  
By people who never put my name on the question.

Illuminara lowered the suspended masonry into a stable arch instead of rebuilding the wall. Fresh air could enter. Oru could see the opening. Emergency fabric sealed the pressure gap around it without closing the way out.

**Illuminara**  
May I enter far enough to listen to the machinery through the floor? Not to your mind. Not to your body unless you show me how.
Oru studied the open arch, the red cord, the city official and the physician whose hands trembled with nine hours of arithmetic.

**Oru**  
You may listen where the stone listens. If you call the sound consent, I will stop speaking.

scenes.title: The Shape of a Breath
paragraphs: *Lower turbine gallery under Oru's chamber · Eight hours before reserve exhaustion*

The gallery smelled of hot oil and mineral rain. Each of Oru's breaths pushed air through six separate turbine trunks. The trunks were not merely pipes. Their old valves turned his slow inhale and faster exhale into a pressure pattern the hospital generators used to stay synchronized.

Illuminara knelt with both hands on the floor. She listened to iron, not to Oru's thoughts. A hairline fault in the fourth trunk clicked every thirty-seven seconds. The giant altered his next breath before the fault could strike.

**Illuminara**  
You have been correcting the machinery.

**Oru**  
Since before Kes's grandmother learned to lie politely.
Kes opened his mouth and then closed it.

**Dr Anik**  
Our manuals call the pressure self-balancing.

**Oru**  
Your manuals call me geological assistance.
Rava ran a finger over a brass plate. Someone had chiseled away the first line. Under the scratches remained three words: CAPTIVE RESPIRATORY PRIME.

**Rava**  
We publish this now.

**Kes**  
If the city hears it while the hospitals are failing, the lower districts will riot.

**Oru**  
They may be angry in the same hour they are useful.

Illuminara traced the pressure rhythm outward while Kes opened the city's archived utility map. Beneath Vale ran compressed-air reservoirs once used by tram lines, now kept half full for freight brakes. Deeper still, geothermal wells heated homes and baths, but their steam bypassed the turbine district because an old mineral separator could not handle pulsed flow. On Kes's map, the abandoned east interchange still held freight locks and timing drums. A second line crossed beneath it: LAUNDRY STERILIZER RETURN—ACTIVE. Maintenance had marked the floor above it WARM IN EVERY SEASON.

Illuminara could see only the outline: tram pressure for the fast exhale, geothermal flow for the slow refill, and the hospital turbines already in place. The missing interval between them still belonged to Oru's body.

**Illuminara**  
The city has enough stored pressure to begin and enough geothermal flow to continue. But the separator floods whenever demand pulses. I do not yet know what his body does that the circuit does not.

**Kes**  
A new separator takes six months.

**Kes**  
East Interchange still has the freight locks, six check valves and the old timing drums. The inventory was written off, not removed.

**Rava**  
And who builds it? The same office that hid his name?

**Illuminara**  
Anyone Oru accepts. Your crews, hospital engineers, city workers. The design belongs to all of them. The test belongs to the patient councils.
Oru's next exhale slowed. The fourth trunk clicked twice.

**Oru**  
You heard the shape. You did not hear the ache.
Illuminara lifted her hands from the floor.

**Illuminara**  
Will you show me where it begins?

Oru guided her without contact. He breathed once while she watched the pressure gauges, then stopped midway. The chamber's south brace pulled against a stone plate beneath his ribs. The machinery required him to twist every exhale around a support installed after the restraints had rusted.

**Oru**  
They say I chose to remain. They do not say the choice hurts in the shape their gratitude prefers.

**Dr Anik**  
How long?

**Oru**  
The city has used my breathing for three hundred years. This brace has hurt for forty-one.
Anik removed the hospital council badge from her coat and set it on the stained floor.

**Dr Anik**  
Then the patient councils have been voting on a lie too.

**Illuminara**  
The bridge must match the turbines without matching your pain. Give me three breaths you choose, with a pause between them. We will record the pressures, not your body. You can end the measurement at any moment.
Oru gave one breath, then another. Before the third, he looked through the open arch at the first strip of daylight to reach the chamber in generations.

**Oru**  
Two are enough. Let the machine learn there is no entitlement to a third.

scenes.title: No One Owns the Door
paragraphs: *Vale assembly rotunda and six linked hospital wards · Six hours before reserve exhaustion*

The erased brass plate filled every public screen. Beside it appeared the first contracts: Oru purchased as a war captive, his name replaced by ENGINE SOURCE NINE. Kes had released the records after Oru demanded that no transition begin under a clean lie.

The rotunda divided before anyone spoke. Open Earth members held red cords. Turbine workers wore blue. Hospital patients appeared from beds through wall-sized links. Oru's voice came through the chamber floor.

**Kes**  
My office concealed the founding records. I signed the last three renewals without asking Oru directly. The archive is public, and I have placed my authority under council review.

**Rava**  
Review is late. The restraint is not.

**Dr Anik**  
Immediate disconnection kills patients before transfer can be completed. I will not call that treatment.
A boy in the north children's ward raised his hand. His name was Pell. A clear tube carried blood from his chest to an oxygenator.

**Pell**  
Is Oru listening?

**Oru**  
Yes.

**Pell**  
Thank you for today. I don't want you to have to do tomorrow.

**Pell**  
I also want you to stay. I know morning has started by the change in your breathing. I know that is not a fair reason.
Oru's fingers tightened once against the chamber floor. The pressure trace carried the movement into every ward.

**Oru**  
I am glad the sound kept you company. I cannot promise to make my body your clock. If I visit, it will be because I chose the road to you.
Oru closed his eyes. The next turbine pulse arrived late, then recovered.

**Rava**  
That is why we disconnect him now. No more compromises made over his body.

**Oru**  
You speak as if the only door out is the one you choose for me.

**Rava**  
I am trying to make sure they cannot choose for you again.

**Oru**  
Then stand beside my door. Do not own the direction I walk through it.
The red cords lowered. Rava's objection did not disappear.

**Rava**  
If you stay while they still depend on you, how can anyone know the choice is free?

**Oru**  
They cannot. That is why the dependence must end before you ask what I choose next.

Illuminara projected the bridge plan. Tram pressure would run the hospitals during the first test. Geothermal steam would refill the reservoirs through a dry chamber assembled at East Interchange. If the bridge failed, Oru's trunks could reconnect in eleven seconds without sealing the open wall.

**Illuminara**  
The proof has three parts. First, all six hospitals run on the bridge for one full hour while Oru's valves are physically open to the chamber, not to the turbines. Second, pressure remains within two percent through an unannounced hospital load change chosen by the patient councils. Third, Oru walks beyond the old restraint line before anyone asks him to return.

A refusal flashed across the tram union's board: no reservoir transfer until the founding archive was public, paused crews were paid, and lower-district delegates controlled two valve seats. Kes moved the executive contingency fund to wages and surrendered the seats. The lower districts did not riot. Their pipe crews arrived with hammers and elected valve keepers. The board turned amber, then green.

**Kes**  
The tram reservoirs will empty in four hours if the geothermal chamber misses its mark.

**Illuminara**  
Then the test fails honestly, the hospitals return to Oru's breathing, and we learn what must change. We do not rename failure liberation.

**Dr Anik**  
The councils require one more condition. If the bridge works only by closing emergency wards, it does not work.

**Rava**  
Open Earth requires independent valve keepers at every trunk and an alarm Oru controls from inside or outside the chamber.

**Oru**  
I require the old support removed before I give another working breath. Not after the crisis. Now.
Kes looked at the clock.

**Kes**  
Removing it costs forty minutes.

**Oru**  
It has cost me forty-one years.

Illuminara did not offer to rip it out alone. She held the chamber roof while turbine workers cut the brace in view of Oru, Rava and the patient councils. Kes carried the first severed piece into the rotunda and laid it beside the erased plate.
When Oru breathed again, the pressure rose four percent with less effort.
The four-percent rise appeared at once on six ward screens. Oru released a long breath that did not drag against iron.

scenes.title: Borrowed Breath
paragraphs: *East Interchange and North Children's Hospital · Two hours before reserve exhaustion*

The temporary manifold occupied the abandoned tram hall: a ring of six salvaged valves, two timing drums and a dry chamber made from freight locks. A strip of floor above the active laundry return stayed warm even before steam entered the system. Illuminara held the warped upper seam together while ordinary welders closed it. She could keep the metal aligned. She could not make a bad circuit breathe.

At North Children's, Pell watched the pressure line climb toward transfer. Dr Anik stood beside his bed. Rava held the manual valve key. Kes had placed the city's master key on the floor beyond his reach.

**Illuminara**  
Oru, we are ready to take the first hospital. You set the count.

**Oru**  
Not ready. The third drum is early.

**Kes**  
The instruments show synchronization.

**Oru**  
The instruments have never had ribs.

Illuminara listened again. The third drum struck at the correct moment, but its valve opened too quickly. Oru's breathing had always cushioned that edge with the slight flex of his chest. A metal bridge would send a hard pressure wave into the oldest hospital turbines.

**Illuminara**  
He is right. Add a water buffer before the third valve.

**Rava**  
The nearest tank is part of the fire line.

**Pell**  
Our roof has a rain cistern.
Anik checked the hospital plan. The cistern was full, isolated and high enough to answer pressure without a pump.

**Dr Anik**  
Use ours. Fire reserve remains above code for three hours.
Rava and two hospital engineers opened the old roof line. The patient council, not Kes, authorized the temporary risk.
The first transfer began. Oru's trunk valve opened to the chamber. East Interchange sent its measured exhale through the north line. The turbine caught it cleanly.
Then the dry chamber flooded.
Mineral water struck the timing drums. Two valves jammed half open. At North Children's the lights dimmed and Pell's oxygenator changed to battery.

**Kes**  
Reconnect Oru.

**Rava**  
Wait. Twenty seconds of battery margin.

**Dr Anik**  
Seventeen now.
Illuminara held the dry chamber above the flood and looked for the wrong assumption. Steam entered dry. Water was condensing after the pressure drop, faster than the drain could carry it.

**Illuminara**  
Oru, what do you do with the cold in the return stroke?

**Oru**  
I keep it in my heels.

**Rava**  
Meaning?

**Oru**  
The return air warms through the lower rock before I draw it again. Your bridge has no heel.
Pell pressed the call switch from his bed.

**Pell**  
The laundry return makes that strip of tram floor warm. Maintenance complains every winter. Can it warm the pipe?
Kes reopened the archived map. The line they had noticed beneath East Interchange was marked obsolete at the manifold but active from two hospital sterilizers.

**Kes**  
We can wrap the return line. Ninety seconds.

**Dr Anik**  
Battery margin is twelve.

**Oru**  
Use one breath of mine. Not because you failed to free me. Because Pell asked the right question.
Rava turned Oru's valve for exactly one cycle. His exhale restored the hospital line while crews cut into the laundry heat pipe. No wall closed. No restraint engaged.

The interruption and rebalancing cost eleven minutes of tram reserve. When Oru's valve closed again, the patient councils reset the one-hour proof clock to zero. The reserve board showed one hour and thirty-two minutes.
The warm return cleared the condensate. East Interchange took the next pulse, then the next. North Children's lights steadied before Pell's battery reached five minutes.

**Pell**  
Did it work?

**Oru**  
The return is warm. The pulse is stable.

**Illuminara**  
The proof starts again now.
She released the seam. The weld held without her.

scenes.title: After the Turbines Let Go
paragraphs: *Oru's open chamber and Vale's western ridge · Dawn after the full-load test*

After the flood the councils reset the clock. They transferred the hospitals in pairs while the tram reserve declined and geothermal refill slowed the loss. Once all six were on the repaired bridge, it carried them for one uninterrupted hour. Midway through that hour the councils changed the load without warning: two sterilizers, a magnetic theatre and every oxygenator in the south ward at once. Pell watched the green lamp beside his blood line hold steady. Anik watched one pressure needle tremble and return; Rava kept her palm above the valve key and did not touch it. Pressure stayed within one point six percent. When the hour ended, the tram reserve board showed eighteen minutes.

Oru's six trunk valves stood open to the chamber. Air moved through them in both directions, useless to the turbines. For the first time since the founding contract, a hospital's survival did not rise and fall with his chest.
Rava removed the last red cord from the doorway and tied it around the public archive case instead.

**Rava**  
The door is yours.

**Oru**  
It always was. Now it leads somewhere.
He rose slowly. Stone dust fell from joints held in one position longer than the city had kept any constitution. Illuminara offered her shoulder and waited.

**Oru**  
Yes.
Turbine workers walked beside him as he placed one foot, then the other, beyond the old restraint line. Kes stood aside. Anik watched the hospital readings and did not ask him to hurry.
His chosen weight settled through her shoulder. Warm stone dust touched her cheek, and joy rose in her, quick and quiet, at being trusted with exactly that much.
Outside, dawn struck the upper plates of Oru's face. He stopped so long that the crowd mistook stillness for uncertainty.

**Oru**  
It is smaller than I remembered.

**Illuminara**  
The sky?

**Oru**  
The city. They built it very large inside my chamber.

He walked to the western ridge, where an unfinished quarry house had been widened overnight by stonecutters, activists and turbine crews. It had no pipes leading to a hospital. Its door opened from either side.
Only after Oru had slept there for six hours did the assembly ask what he wanted next.

**Kes**  
The bridge can carry the hospitals, but it closes two tram lines and most night foundry work. Permanent geothermal redundancy takes six weeks. The city has no claim on your help.

**Rava**  
Open Earth will keep independent watch whether you return or not.

**Dr Anik**  
The patient councils will fund the redundancy before any ceremonial project. We also request a direct seat for you, not a geological advisory category.
Oru looked at Illuminara.

**Oru**  
What do you want me to choose?

**Illuminara**  
Nothing that proves I was right. I want the hospitals safe, the old crime impossible to hide, and you able to change your mind without punishment.
A smile moved through the seams of his face like light entering a canyon.

**Oru**  
Then I will give one shift each third day for six weeks. Four hours, never sleeping in the chamber, and Rava keeps the valve key. Not because Vale needs my body. Because the children asked me to stay until the replacement grows roots.

**Rava**  
I still dislike it.

**Oru**  
Good. Stand beside the door.

Kes signed the transition charter, then signed his resignation and the release of every founding record. The assembly created Oru's independent home and an unconditional right to disconnect that no emergency declaration could suspend. None of that erased the original enslavement. It changed what the city could demand next.

Six weeks later the permanent geothermal ring took the hospital load. Oru did not attend its dedication. Pell's bed had been wheeled into the North Children's courtyard, where Oru was teaching patients how to hear faults in stone through the soles of their feet.

**Pell**  
Are you a doctor now?

**Oru**  
No.
He set one broad finger against the courtyard paving. A pump beneath the hospital slab clicked out of rhythm.

**Oru**  
I am someone who knows what a machine sounds like when it hurts.
Pell placed his bare foot beside Oru's hand. Far below, a pump skipped once; both of them looked up at the same instant.

critic_line: Oru, a stone giant whose breathing has powered six hospitals for three hundred years, is neither dragged out nor kept in: Illuminara listens where he can feel it, the city's crews and patients build a bridge he corrects, and he leaves the chamber by his own step to a home of his own while every patient stays powered.

shared_strengths: Humane, dialogue-heavy, with a fresh ethical hook: rescue must not become another order. Clever engineering payoffs (Pell's warm laundry floor, the heel). Dense infrastructure exposition and a tidy, over-resolved, slightly schematic cast may lose some readers midway.

A compelling moral dilemma becomes concrete through tense, character-rich dialogue and collaborative engineering. Oru’s dry authority, Pell’s compassion and the recurring door metaphor are memorable. Some infrastructure exposition slows the middle, and the resolution is unusually tidy, but the humane treatment of consent, dependency and repair should strongly satisfy this audience.

translation_sl.title: VELIKAN, KI NI HOTEL BITI REŠEN
translation_sl.deck: Illuminara razpre zasuto strojnico in najde Oruja, kamnitega velikana, čigar dihanje poganja šest bolnišnic. Oditi noče. Do ustavitve poškodovanih turbin je devet ur; zaščititi mora bolnike, razkriti stari zločin mesta in poskrbeti, da njegovo bivanje tam ne bo več nujno — ne da bi osvoboditev spremenila v še en ukaz, namenjen njemu.
translation_sl.shape: Pet prizorov vodi od Illuminarine zmotne rešitve in Orujeve zavrnitve prek telesnega poslušanja, ki razkrije, kako si lahko njegovo dihanje ter pozabljeni mestni sistemi stisnjenega zraka in geotermalne energije delijo isti tlačni ritem, do javnega soočenja, v katerem Oru zavrne tako uradno prikrivanje kot aktivistično lastninjenje njegove svobode. Spodletel prenos bolnišnice prisili Oruja, bolnike, ekipe in aktiviste, da premostitev popravijo skupaj. Ko vseh šest bolnišnic deluje brez njegovega telesa, Oru svobodno izbere omejeno prehodno delo, dobi samostojen dom in se pozneje vrne kot zdravilec, ne kot motor.

scenes.title: Zid, ki se je odprl
paragraphs: *Kotlovnica devet pod mestom Vale · Devet ur do izčrpanja bolnišnične rezerve*

Illuminara je iz zasute stene iztrgala zadnje železno rebro in ujela tristo ton razpokanega zidu, preden bi se zrušil navznoter. Mimo nje je v dvorano, zgrajeno okoli spečega telesa, planil hladen zrak.

Velikan je meril štirideset metrov. Temne kamnite plošče na njegovih prsih so se dvigale in spuščale. Z vsakim vdihom se je stisnilo šest bronastih mehov ob njem. Daleč zgoraj je šest bolnišnic prejemalo njegov utrip po ceveh, starejših od vsakega živečega inženirja.
Obroči za vklenitev okoli njegovih zapestij so že pred rodovi prerjaveli in se razprli. Njihove brazgotine ne.

Rava Sen, vodja kolektiva Odprta zemlja, je z rdečo osvobodilno vrvico okoli roke splezala čez razbiti prag. Za njo sta prišla direktor Kes iz mestnega urada za energijo in dr. Anik Ilyan, ki jo je izvolilo šest svetov bolnikov.

**Rava**  
Oru, zid je odprt. Lahko prideš ven.
Velikanove oči so se odprle kakor dve svetilki za od dežja potemnelim steklom.

**Oru**  
Zaprite ga.
Tlačni alarm je zatulil. Illuminara je čutila, kako iz poškodovane dvorane uhaja gost zrak, zaradi katerega so mehovi delovali učinkovito. Vsak naslednji dih je dal manj sile od prejšnjega.

**Illuminara**  
Mislila sem, da je to delujoč zapor. Odprla sem ga, preden sem te vprašala.

**Oru**  
Da.
Počakala je. Opravičilo, ki bi hitelo proti odpuščanju, bi od njega zahtevalo le še, naj nosi tudi njeno nelagodje.

**Illuminara**  
Žal mi je. Popravila bom, kar sem zlomila. Brez tvojega dovoljenja se te ne bom več dotaknila.

**Kes**  
Zahodnega tesnila ne moremo pravočasno obnoviti. Ob sedanjem uhajanju bodo bolnišnične turbine čez devet ur padle pod varno moč.

**Rava**  
Potem evakuirajte bolnišnice. Ne bomo ga vrnili v kletko zato, ker je vaše mesto suženjstvo naredilo priročno.

**Dr Anik**  
Štiristo bolnikov ni mogoče premakniti. Dvaintrideset jih je priključenih na krvne oksigenatorje. Temu lahko rečete priročnost, ko jih boste odnesli skozi zgornje predore.
Rava je trznila, vendar ni odstopila.

**Rava**  
In koliko stoletij mu predpisujete še?
Oru je eno dlan položil na tla dvorane. Turbine so odgovorile z nizkim, enakomernim tresljajem.

**Oru**  
Ničesar ne predpisujem. Nisem vaš bolnik.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj želiš v naslednjih devetih urah?

**Oru**  
Da otroci dihajo. Da je resnica izrečena. Da nihče mojega odhoda ne uporabi kot dokaz, da me je končno razumel.
Kes je gledal odprte okove namesto Oruja.

**Kes**  
Sedanja ureditev je bila potrjena triinosemdesetkrat.

**Oru**  
Potrdili so jo ljudje, ki mojega imena niso nikoli zapisali v vprašanje.

Illuminara je viseče zidovje spustila v stabilen lok, namesto da bi zid znova zgradila. Svež zrak je lahko vstopal. Oru je videl odprtino. Zasilna tkanina je zatesnila tlačno režo okoli nje, ne da bi zaprla izhod.

**Illuminara**  
Smem vstopiti dovolj daleč, da skozi tla poslušam stroje? Ne tvojih misli. Ne tvojega telesa, razen če mi sam pokažeš kako.
Oru je premeril odprti lok, rdečo vrvico, mestnega uradnika in zdravnico, ki so se ji roke tresle od deveturne računice.

**Oru**  
Poslušaš lahko tam, kjer posluša kamen. Če boš zvok imenovala privolitev, bom nehal govoriti.

scenes.title: Oblika diha
paragraphs: *Spodnja turbinska galerija pod Orujevo dvorano · Osem ur do izčrpanja rezerve*

V galeriji je dišalo po vročem olju in mineralnem dežju. Vsak Orujev dih je potisnil zrak skozi šest ločenih turbinskih vodov. Vodi niso bili le cevi. Njihovi stari ventili so njegov počasni vdih in hitrejši izdih spreminjali v tlačni vzorec, s katerim so bolnišnični generatorji ostajali usklajeni.

Illuminara je pokleknila z obema dlanema na tleh. Poslušala je železo, ne Orujevih misli. Lasasta razpoka v četrtem vodu je kliknila vsakih sedemintrideset sekund. Velikan je naslednji dih prilagodil, še preden bi razpoka lahko udarila.

**Illuminara**  
Ves čas popravljaš delovanje strojev.

**Oru**  
Od časa, preden se je Kesova babica naučila vljudno lagati.
Kes je odprl usta in jih nato zaprl.

**Dr Anik**  
Naši priročniki tlak opisujejo kot samouravnalnega.

**Oru**  
Vaši priročniki mene opisujejo kot geološko pomoč.
Rava je s prstom zdrsnila čez medeninasto ploščico. Nekdo je izklesal prvo vrstico. Pod praskami so ostale tri besede: UJETNIŠKI DIHALNI POGON.

**Rava**  
To objavimo zdaj.

**Kes**  
Če mesto to izve med odpovedovanjem bolnišnic, se bodo spodnja okrožja uprla.

**Oru**  
V isti uri so lahko jezni in koristni.

Illuminara je sledila tlačnemu ritmu navzven, medtem ko je Kes odprl arhivski zemljevid mestnih vodov. Pod mestom Vale so tekli rezervoarji stisnjenega zraka, nekoč namenjeni tramvajskim progam, zdaj pa napol polni za tovorne zavore. Globlje so geotermalni vodnjaki ogrevali domove in kopeli, vendar je njihova para obšla turbinsko okrožje, ker stari ločevalnik mineralov ni zmogel pulznega toka. Na Kesovem zemljevidu so v opuščenem Vzhodnem križišču še vedno bile tovorne zapornice in časovni bobni. Pod njim je prečkala druga cev: POVRATEK PRALNIŠKEGA STERILIZATORJA — DEJAVEN. Vzdrževalci so tla nad njo označili z VSE LETNE ČASE TOPLA.

Illuminara je videla le obris: tramvajski tlak za hitri izdih, geotermalni tok za počasno polnjenje in že postavljene bolnišnične turbine. Manjkajoči razmik med njimi je še vedno pripadal Orujevemu telesu.

**Illuminara**  
Mesto ima dovolj shranjenega tlaka za začetek in dovolj geotermalnega toka za nadaljevanje. Toda ločevalnik poplavi ob vsakem sunku porabe. Še ne vem, kaj naredi njegovo telo, česar vezje ne.

**Kes**  
Za nov ločevalnik potrebujemo šest mesecev.

**Kes**  
Vzhodno križišče ima še vedno tovorne zapornice, šest nepovratnih ventilov in stare časovne bobne. Inventar so odpisali, ne odstranili.

**Rava**  
In kdo ga bo zgradil? Isti urad, ki je skril njegovo ime?

**Illuminara**  
Kdorkoli, ki ga Oru sprejme. Vaše ekipe, bolnišnični inženirji, mestni delavci. Zasnova pripada vsem. Preizkus pripada svetom bolnikov.
Orujev naslednji izdih se je upočasnil. Četrti vod je dvakrat kliknil.

**Oru**  
Slišala si obliko. Bolečine nisi.
Illuminara je dvignila dlani s tal.

**Illuminara**  
Mi boš pokazal, kje se začne?

Oru jo je vodil brez dotika. Enkrat je vdihnil, medtem ko je opazovala merilnike tlaka, nato pa se je na polovici ustavil. Južna opora dvorane je vlekla kamnito ploščo pod njegovimi rebri. Stroji so od njega zahtevali, da vsak izdih zavije okoli opore, nameščene po tem, ko so okovi prerjaveli.

**Oru**  
Pravijo, da sem se odločil ostati. Ne povedo, da izbira boli v obliki, ki jo ima njihova hvaležnost najraje.

**Dr Anik**  
Kako dolgo?

**Oru**  
Mesto moje dihanje uporablja tristo let. Ta opora me boli enainštirideset.
Anik je z ogrinjala snela značko sveta bolnikov in jo položila na umazana tla.

**Dr Anik**  
Potem so tudi sveti bolnikov glasovali o laži.

**Illuminara**  
Premostitev se mora ujemati s turbinami, ne da bi posnemala tvojo bolečino. Daj mi tri dihe po svoji izbiri, s premorom med njimi. Zabeležili bomo tlake, ne tvojega telesa. Merjenje lahko kadarkoli končaš.
Oru je dal en dih, nato drugega. Pred tretjim je skozi odprti lok pogledal prvi trak dnevne svetlobe, ki je po rodovih dosegel dvorano.

**Oru**  
Dva sta dovolj. Naj se stroj nauči, da do tretjega nima pravice.

scenes.title: Nihče si ne lasti vrat
paragraphs: *Rotunda zbora mesta Vale in šest povezanih bolnišničnih oddelkov · Šest ur do izčrpanja rezerve*

Izbrisana medeninasta ploščica je napolnila vsak javni zaslon. Ob njej so se pojavile prve pogodbe: Oru, kupljen kot vojni ujetnik, njegovo ime nadomeščeno z POGONSKI VIR DEVET. Kes je zapise objavil, potem ko je Oru zahteval, da se noben prehod ne začne pod očiščeno lažjo.

Rotunda se je razdelila, še preden je kdo spregovoril. Člani Odprte zemlje so držali rdeče vrvice. Turbinski delavci so nosili modro. Bolniki so se iz postelj prikazali prek povezav v velikosti stene. Orujev glas je prihajal skozi tla dvorane.

**Kes**  
Moj urad je prikril ustanovne zapise. Zadnja tri podaljšanja sem podpisal, ne da bi Oruja neposredno vprašal. Arhiv je javen, svojo pristojnost pa sem predal v pregled svetu.

**Rava**  
Pregled zamuja. Prisiljevanje ne.

**Dr Anik**  
Takojšnji odklop ubije bolnike, preden lahko končamo prenos. Tega ne bom imenovala zdravljenje.
Deček na severnem otroškem oddelku je dvignil roko. Ime mu je bilo Pell. Prozorna cev je kri iz njegovih prsi vodila v oksigenator.

**Pell**  
Oru posluša?

**Oru**  
Da.

**Pell**  
Hvala za danes. Nočem, da bi moral to početi tudi jutri.

**Pell**  
Prav tako hočem, da ostaneš. Po spremembi tvojega dihanja vem, da se je začelo jutro. Vem, da to ni pošten razlog.
Orujevi prsti so se enkrat napeli ob tla dvorane. Tlačna sled je gib prenesla v vse oddelke.

**Oru**  
Vesel sem, da ti je zvok delal družbo. Ne morem obljubiti, da bo moje telo tvoja ura. Če te obiščem, bo zato, ker sem sam izbral pot do tebe.
Oru je zaprl oči. Naslednji turbinski sunek je prišel pozno, nato pa se je popravil.

**Rava**  
Zato ga odklopimo zdaj. Nič več kompromisov na račun njegovega telesa.

**Oru**  
Govoriš, kakor da so edina vrata ven tista, ki jih zame izbereš ti.

**Rava**  
Poskušam preprečiti, da bi lahko znova izbirali namesto tebe.

**Oru**  
Potem stoj ob mojih vratih. Ne lasti si smeri, v katero grem skoznje.
Rdeče vrvice so se spustile. Ravino nasprotovanje ni izginilo.

**Rava**  
Če ostaneš, ko so še odvisni od tebe, kako bo lahko kdorkoli vedel, da je izbira svobodna?

**Oru**  
Ne morejo. Zato se mora odvisnost končati, preden me vprašate, kaj izberem potem.

Illuminara je projicirala načrt premostitve. Tramvajski tlak bi med prvim preizkusom poganjal bolnišnice. Geotermalna para bi rezervoarje polnila skozi suho komoro, sestavljeno v Vzhodnem križišču. Če bi premostitev odpovedala, bi se Orujevi vodi lahko znova priključili v enajstih sekundah, ne da bi zaprli odprti zid.

**Illuminara**  
Dokaz ima tri dele. Prvič, vseh šest bolnišnic eno polno uro deluje na premostitvi, medtem ko so Orujevi ventili fizično odprti v dvorano, ne proti turbinam. Drugič, tlak ob nenapovedani spremembi bolnišnične porabe, ki jo izberejo sveti bolnikov, ostane znotraj dveh odstotkov. Tretjič, Oru stopi čez staro črto okovov, preden ga kdorkoli prosi, naj se vrne.

Na tabli tramvajskega sindikata je zasvetila zavrnitev: nobenega prenosa iz rezervoarjev, dokler ustanovni arhiv ni javen, ustavljene ekipe plačane in predstavniki spodnjih okrožij ne nadzorujejo dveh ventilskih sedežev. Kes je izvršni rezervni sklad prenesel v plače in prepustil sedeža. Spodnja okrožja se niso uprla. Njihove cevne ekipe so prispele s kladivi in izvoljenimi varuhi ventilov. Tabla je postala jantarna, nato zelena.

**Kes**  
Tramvajski rezervoarji bodo prazni v štirih urah, če geotermalna komora zgreši cilj.

**Illuminara**  
Potem preizkus pošteno spodleti, bolnišnice se vrnejo na Orujevo dihanje in izvemo, kaj je treba spremeniti. Spodrsljaja ne bomo preimenovali v osvoboditev.

**Dr Anik**  
Sveti zahtevajo še en pogoj. Če premostitev deluje samo ob zaprtju urgentnih oddelkov, potem ne deluje.

**Rava**  
Odprta zemlja zahteva neodvisne varuhe ventilov na vsakem vodu in alarm, ki ga Oru nadzira iz dvorane ali zunaj nje.

**Oru**  
Zahtevam odstranitev stare opore, preden dam še en delovni dih. Ne po krizi. Zdaj.
Kes je pogledal na uro.

**Kes**  
Odstranitev stane štirideset minut.

**Oru**  
Mene je stala enainštirideset let.

Illuminara se ni ponudila, da jo iztrga sama. Držala je strop dvorane, medtem ko so turbinski delavci oporo rezali pred Orujem, Ravo in sveti bolnikov. Kes je prvi odrezani kos odnesel v rotundo in ga položil ob izbrisano ploščico.
Ko je Oru znova vdihnil, se je tlak z manj napora dvignil za štiri odstotke.
Štiriodstotni dvig se je takoj pojavil na zaslonih šestih oddelkov. Oru je izdihnil dolg dih, ki ni več drgnil ob železo.

scenes.title: Izposojeni dih
paragraphs: *Vzhodno križišče in Severna otroška bolnišnica · Dve uri do izčrpanja rezerve*

Začasni razdelilnik je zasedel opuščeno tramvajsko dvorano: obroč šestih rešenih ventilov, dva časovna bobna in suha komora iz tovornih zapornic. Pas tal nad dejavnim pralniškim povratkom je ostal topel, še preden je v sistem vstopila para. Illuminara je držala zviti zgornji spoj, medtem ko so ga navadni varilci zaprli. Kovino je lahko držala poravnano. Slabega vezja ni mogla pripraviti do dihanja.

V Severni otroški bolnišnici je Pell opazoval, kako se tlačna črta vzpenja proti prenosu. Dr. Anik je stala ob njegovi postelji. Rava je držala ključ ročnega ventila. Kes je glavni mestni ključ položil na tla izven svojega dosega.

**Illuminara**  
Oru, pripravljeni smo prevzeti prvo bolnišnico. Ti določiš štetje.

**Oru**  
Niste pripravljeni. Tretji boben prehiteva.

**Kes**  
Instrumenti kažejo usklajenost.

**Oru**  
Instrumenti nikoli niso imeli reber.

Illuminara je znova prisluhnila. Tretji boben je udaril ob pravem času, vendar se je njegov ventil odprl prehitro. Orujevo dihanje je ta rob vedno ublažilo z rahlim upogibom njegovih prsi. Kovinska premostitev bi poslala trd tlačni val v najstarejše bolnišnične turbine.

**Illuminara**  
Prav ima. Pred tretji ventil dodajte vodni blažilnik.

**Rava**  
Najbližji rezervoar je del požarnega voda.

**Pell**  
Naša streha ima deževnico.
Anik je preverila načrt bolnišnice. Cisterna je bila polna, ločena in dovolj visoko, da je lahko odgovorila na tlak brez črpalke.

**Dr Anik**  
Uporabite našo. Požarna rezerva ostane tri ure nad predpisanim minimumom.
Rava in dva bolnišnična inženirja so odprli star strešni vod. Začasno tveganje je odobril svet bolnikov, ne Kes.
Prvi prenos se je začel. Orujev ventil voda se je odprl v dvorano. Vzhodno križišče je svoj odmerjeni izdih poslalo po severnem vodu. Turbina ga je gladko ujela.
Nato je suha komora poplavila.
Mineralna voda je udarila ob časovne bobne. Dva ventila sta se zagozdila napol odprta. V Severni otroški bolnišnici so luči potemnele, Pellov oksigenator pa je prešel na baterijo.

**Kes**  
Znova priključite Oruja.

**Rava**  
Počakajte. Dvajset sekund baterijske rezerve.

**Dr Anik**  
Zdaj sedemnajst.
Illuminara je držala suho komoro nad poplavo in iskala napačno predpostavko. Para je vstopala suha. Voda je po padcu tlaka kondenzirala hitreje, kot jo je odtok lahko odvedel.

**Illuminara**  
Oru, kaj narediš z mrazom v povratnem hodu?

**Oru**  
Zadržim ga v petah.

**Rava**  
Kaj to pomeni?

**Oru**  
Povratni zrak se ogreje skozi spodnjo skalo, preden ga znova vdihnem. Vaša premostitev nima pete.
Pell je iz postelje pritisnil klicno stikalo.

**Pell**  
Pralniški povratek ogreva tisti pas tramvajskih tal. Vzdrževalci se pritožujejo vsako zimo. Lahko ogreje cev?
Kes je znova odprl arhivski zemljevid. Vod, ki so ga opazili pod Vzhodnim križiščem, je bil pri razdelilniku označen kot zastarel, vendar še dejaven od dveh bolnišničnih sterilizatorjev.

**Kes**  
Povratni vod lahko ovijemo. Devetdeset sekund.

**Dr Anik**  
Baterijska rezerva je dvanajst.

**Oru**  
Uporabite en moj dih. Ne zato, ker vam me ni uspelo osvoboditi. Zato, ker je Pell postavil pravo vprašanje.
Rava je Orujev ventil odprla za natanko en cikel. Njegov izdih je obnovil bolnišnični vod, medtem ko so ekipe zarezale v cev pralniške toplote. Noben zid se ni zaprl. Nobena vez ni prijela.

Prekinitev in ponovno uravnoteženje sta stala enajst minut tramvajske rezerve. Ko se je Orujev ventil znova zaprl, so sveti bolnikov enourno dokazno uro ponastavili na nič. Tabla rezerve je kazala uro in dvaintrideset minut.
Topli povratek je odstranil kondenzat. Vzhodno križišče je prevzelo naslednji sunek, nato naslednjega. Luči v Severni otroški bolnišnici so se ustalile, preden je Pellova baterija padla na pet minut.

**Pell**  
Je uspelo?

**Oru**  
Povratek je topel. Sunek je stabilen.

**Illuminara**  
Dokaz se znova začne zdaj.
Spustila je spoj. Zvar je držal brez nje.

scenes.title: Ko so turbine popustile
paragraphs: *Orujeva odprta dvorana in zahodni greben mesta Vale · Zora po preizkusu polne obremenitve*

Po poplavi so sveti uro ponastavili. Bolnišnice so prenesli v parih, medtem ko je tramvajska rezerva upadala, geotermalno polnjenje pa je izgubo upočasnjevalo. Ko je bilo vseh šest priključenih na popravljeno premostitev, jih je ta brez prekinitve poganjala eno uro. Na polovici te ure so sveti brez opozorila spremenili obremenitev: dva sterilizatorja, magnetni operacijski prostor in vsi oksigenatorji na južnem oddelku hkrati. Pell je opazoval, kako zelena lučka ob njegovi krvni cevi ostaja prižgana. Anik je gledala, kako se ena tlačna igla zatrese in vrne; Rava je dlan držala nad ključem ventila in se ga ni dotaknila. Tlak je ostal znotraj ene cele šest desetinke odstotka. Ko se je ura iztekla, je tabla tramvajske rezerve kazala osemnajst minut.

Orujevih šest ventilov vodov je stalo odprtih proti dvorani. Zrak je skoznje tekel v obe smeri, za turbine neuporaben. Prvič po ustanovni pogodbi preživetje bolnišnice ni naraščalo in padalo z njegovimi prsmi.
Rava je z vrat snela zadnjo rdečo vrvico in jo namesto tega zavezala okoli javnega arhivskega zaboja.

**Rava**  
Vrata so tvoja.

**Oru**  
Vedno so bila. Zdaj nekam vodijo.
Počasi je vstal. Kamniti prah je padal iz sklepov, ki so bili v enem položaju dlje, kot je mesto ohranilo katerokoli ustavo. Illuminara mu je ponudila ramo in počakala.

**Oru**  
Da.
Turbinski delavci so hodili ob njem, ko je najprej eno, nato drugo nogo postavil čez staro črto okovov. Kes je stopil vstran. Anik je spremljala bolnišnične meritve in ga ni prosila, naj pohiti.
Teža, ki jo je izbral, se ji je spustila skozi ramo. Topel kamniti prah se je dotaknil njenega lica, v njej pa se je hitro in tiho dvignilo veselje, ker ji je zaupal natanko toliko.
Zunaj je zora zadela zgornje plošče Orujevega obraza. Ustavil se je tako dolgo, da je množica mirovanje zamenjala za negotovost.

**Oru**  
Manjše je, kot sem se spominjal.

**Illuminara**  
Nebo?

**Oru**  
Mesto. Znotraj moje dvorane so ga zgradili zelo velikega.

Odšel je na zahodni greben, kjer so kamnoseki, aktivisti in turbinske ekipe čez noč razširili nedokončano kamnolomsko hišo. Nobena cev iz nje ni vodila v bolnišnico. Njena vrata so se odpirala z obeh strani.
Šele potem ko je Oru tam spal šest ur, ga je skupščina vprašala, kaj želi naprej.

**Kes**  
Premostitev lahko poganja bolnišnice, vendar zapre dve tramvajski progi in večino nočnega livarskega dela. Trajna geotermalna redundanca zahteva šest tednov. Mesto nima nobene pravice do tvoje pomoči.

**Rava**  
Odprta zemlja bo ohranila neodvisen nadzor, ne glede na to, ali se vrneš.

**Dr Anik**  
Sveti bolnikov bodo redundanco financirali pred vsakim slovesnim projektom. Zate zahtevamo tudi neposreden sedež, ne kategorije geološkega svetovalca.
Oru je pogledal Illuminari.

**Oru**  
Kaj želiš, da izberem?

**Illuminara**  
Ničesar, kar dokazuje, da sem imela prav. Želim varne bolnišnice, stari zločin, ki ga ni mogoče skriti, in tvojo možnost, da si brez kazni premisliš.
Nasmeh se je premaknil skozi šive njegovega obraza kakor svetloba, ki vstopi v kanjon.

**Oru**  
Potem bom šest tednov dal eno izmeno vsak tretji dan. Štiri ure, nikoli ne bom spal v dvorani, Rava pa obdrži ključ ventila. Ne zato, ker Vale potrebuje moje telo. Zato, ker so me otroci prosili, naj ostanem, dokler nadomestilo ne požene korenin.

**Rava**  
Še vedno mi ni všeč.

**Oru**  
Dobro. Stoj ob vratih.

Kes je podpisal prehodno listino, nato še svoj odstop in izpustitev vseh ustanovnih zapisov. Skupščina je ustvarila Orujev samostojen dom in brezpogojno pravico do odklopa, ki je ni mogla razveljaviti nobena razglasitev izrednih razmer. Nič od tega ni izbrisalo prvotnega suženjstva. Spremenilo je, kaj lahko mesto zahteva naslednjič.

Šest tednov pozneje je trajni geotermalni obroč prevzel bolnišnično obremenitev. Oru se njegove otvoritve ni udeležil. Pellovo posteljo so odpeljali na dvorišče Severne otroške bolnišnice, kjer je Oru bolnike učil, kako skozi podplate slišati napake v kamnu.

**Pell**  
Si zdaj zdravnik?

**Oru**  
Ne.
En širok prst je položil na tlak dvorišča. Črpalka pod bolnišnično ploščo je kliknila iz ritma.

**Oru**  
Sem nekdo, ki ve, kako zveni stroj, ko ga boli.
Pell je boso nogo položil ob Orujevo dlan. Daleč spodaj je črpalka enkrat preskočila; oba sta v istem hipu pogledala navzgor.

translation_sl.critic_line: Oru, kamniti velikan, čigar dihanje je tri stoletja poganjalo šest bolnišnic, ni niti odvlečen ven niti zadržan: Illuminara posluša tam, kjer lahko tudi sam čuti, mestne ekipe in bolniki zgradijo premostitev, ki jo pomaga popraviti, sam pa z lastnim korakom zapusti dvorano in odide v svoj dom, medtem ko vsi bolniki ostanejo preskrbljeni z energijo.
